editorial.headline: Environmental Public-Service Administration Is Closed to Foreign Investment
editorial.standfirst: This is a public-administration activity for environmental programmes and policy—not an opening for foreign registration nationally or in Bali.
editorial.body:
Environmental public-service administration is the work of organising the public side of environmental policy and programmes. Its scope reaches public administration for environmental-service programmes, related public policy on research, development and funding, drinking-water provision, waste collection and disposal programmes, and environmental-protection programmes. The common thread is administration: setting, coordinating and running public programmes—not carrying out the underlying operational work itself.

That distinction makes the intended registrant unusually clear. This is a government-service activity, centred on public administration rather than a conventional commercial service line. The slim record names no business scales as open to it. It therefore offers no basis for saying that any particular micro, small, medium or large scale is available; the meaningful frame is the public-administrative function set out in the scope.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is closed. The stated foreign-ownership ceiling is 0%, so there is no foreign equity stake to describe as available within this activity. That is a substantive limit, not a technical footnote: the record’s national classification is TERTUTUP, with its cited basis in Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. A foreign investor should read the activity first as a public-administration category and then as one that is closed to PMA registration nationwide.

Bali does not soften that answer. A foreigner cannot register this activity in Bali today: its Bali PMA status is also TERTUTUP and the record marks it blocked. The reason, however, matters. Bali’s island-wide, permanent low- and medium-low-risk PMA moratorium does not apply here, because this activity is recorded as medium-high/high risk. Its Bali position still calls for verification at the specific address. In short, Bali’s closure should not be misread as a moratorium case, nor as an opening merely because the moratorium does not apply.
